text.p: Stockbroker Wilson HTM Ltd recommended Southern Pacific Petroleum NL and its stablemate Central Pacific Minerals NL as "buys" following further progress at the group's Stuart oil shale project in north Queensland.

"Substantial scope exists for further revaluation of SPP and CPM's share price as development of Stage One of the Stuart deposit progresses," Wilson's director of resource research, Phil Hutchings said in a report.
SPP's share price at the time of last Friday's report stood at A$4.15 and CPM at $10.
The size of the oil shale project was such that SPP/CPM controlled oil reserves similar to the remaining proved oil reserves of the United States, Hutchings said.
He said the Stuart energy co-venturers which also included Canadian energy group Suncor Inc have placed a cost estimate of A$250 million on construction of Stage One of the oil shale project.
"This step is the final milestone leading to financial close of the SPP/CPM/Suncor joint venture," he said.
"We now expect the joint venture to be finalised this quarter with a go-ahead for construction of Stage One plant expected by the end of March," Hutchings said.
By 0245 GMT (1.45 p.m.) on Monday, SPP shares were at A$4.12, unchanged on Friday's close, and CPM at A$10.50, up 50 cents.
